description: Sunburn is an abiotic environmental condition resulting from intense direct ultraviolet solar radiation and high heat exposure, not a pathogen or infectious disease.
symptoms: Reddish, brownish, or bleached bronze discoloration on sun-exposed upper surfaces
Leaves may appear deflated, dry, or leathery in heavily exposed zones
Symptoms occur uniformly on sunlight-facing leaf aspects rather than as random circular spots

sanitation.step: Do not treat with fungicides or bactericides; sunburn is purely an abiotic physiological stress.
Severely desiccated, crispy leaves that have entirely collapsed may be gently pruned at the base if desired for plant aesthetics.
sources: Horticultural Management of Abiotic Plant Injuries

cultural.step: Protect plant from harsh, unshaded midday sun (11 AM to 4 PM); move to bright, indirect sunlight or deploy shade cloth (30-50% shade).
Acclimate plants gradually to increased light intensity over 2 to 3 weeks rather than abrupt relocation.

precautions.step: Never apply chemical sprays or foliar fertilizers during high-temperature midday sun, as this exacerbates cellular leaf scorch.
sources: Agricultural Chemical Safety and Application Guide
